entry_points.text: Negative cookies pass as errors, others succeed with one smallest valid; surface is provider table plus wrappers for prep, submit, status and control with validation, plus acquisition.
Early bring-up exposes unconditional hooks for boot snapshot, trace init, module init and module release.

exports.text: Noncoherent allocation returns kernel address or null; single mapping rejects remappable memory via page plus offset; table unmap uses stored list with original count; ranged sync uses base plus offset; plain forms use zero attributes.
Coherent alloc and free carry no-warning only when requested, managed alloc preserves hint; write-combining alloc, free and mmap always request write-combining while preserving suppression.

Slave prep prefers combined configure-plus-prepare, else separate config then plain scatter-gather; single forms build one-element lists; cyclic, interleaved and copy validate channel, provider and op.

Pause and terminate delegate when present else fail; sync terminate uses async then sleeping sync; status forwards cookie and state, submit calls stored callback, issue triggers provider, completion polls cookies.

Named request reports missing device, release inert, caps query unavailable; ack sets, clears and tests flag; reuse needs advertised support; slave config delegates or fails; direction maps four values plus invalid.
Without remapping parser succeeds without effect and init reports missing device; without tracing registration, lookup, location and symbols collapse to failure or empty.

hazards.text: Remappable single mapping warns once and yields error; segment updates without params warn once and preserve; linkage without switching faults; wrappers check only absence; sync may sleep; max-parity traps on bad flags.
Nesting counter is per-CPU and needs preemption or interrupts disabled, with debug warning in one build; global tracing can be forced off with save around critical sections.
Prep, issue, status, locking, error-pointer, bit, scatter, sleep and interrupt-state helpers are external; callers must not assume in-dossier implementations.

invariants.text: Routed build disables IOVA use, allocation and sync with negative or unsupported results; metadata attach fails invalid and pointer query yields absent.
One build reports no sync need with inert single and probe operations; other reports need unless skipping allowed, with sync and probing effective only under need.
Mask falls back to 32-bit; coherent update needs prior streaming success; size, boundary and align fall back to 64K, all-ones and zero, size update without params ignored after warning.

Unmap either stores address plus 32-bit length or returns zero with inert writes while checking owner; linkage faults without switching else keeps mutual links; unmap attach records state or is inert.

Parity continuation is bit fifteen with set helper; plain max when supported or unrequested, minus one for disabled-parity continuation and minus three for other; gap picks direction, generic or zero.

Iteration starts at head via RCU to dedicated marker without blocking writers; stack read succeeds only on same thread else zero; jump uses low address bit in one build; return-address availability is build dependent.

locks.text: Channel config and prep share one interrupt-aware spin lock as prep may run in completion; neighbor exclusion inert without switching else mutual exclusion; safe prep locks only fallback path.
Unit list and scope arrays traverse under RCU with guard met while global lock held or during boot; active scope variant skips empty slots.
Operation chain and filters read under RCU lock-free; filter changes serialize on per-hash regex mutex.

state_machines.text: Completed and failed are terminal, in-progress, paused and out-of-order are not; outcome success versus source failure, destination failure and abort always with residual; residue limited to advertised descriptor, segment or burst precision.
Use moves prep to submission via callback, issue, cookie polling with last and used, then terminate plus sync.

Site keeps address and flags with high-bit states and low-bit refcount; iteration filters by filter, notrace, probe, module, enabled, touched and address; sharing uses enable-self, enable-peer and disable-peer commands.

structs.text: Channel holds device and slave linkage, cookies, identity with device object and name, list linkage, per-CPU accounting, client counts, router data and private context; descriptor holds cookie, flags, address, channel, submit and free hooks, callbacks, unmap link, metadata mode and neighbor links; progress holds last, used, residue and in-flight.

Slave programming gives orientation, addresses, widths, bursts, windows, flow selector and blob pointer plus length; caps give width masks, directions, burst bounds, commands, residue precision and reuse; interleaved gives starts, orientation, selectors, frames and trailing chunks; vector pairs address with length.

Unmap holds mapped count widened under RAID, subcounts, device link, refcount with length and trailing addresses; metadata attach, pointer with extents and length update; routing pairs predicate with table of names plus selector; router pairs device with release.

Provider holds refcount, counts, lists, filter, cap mask, metadata modes, limits, alignments, identity, backing device, owner, allocator and peripheral caps; ops cover alloc, preparations, query, config, pause, resume, terminate, sync, status, issue, release and debug.

Unit keeps list linkage, firmware header, register start and extent, scope pointer plus count, segment, three marks and IOMMU pointer; scope binds device, bus and function; hotplug carries device, event, bus, segment, level and path; interrupt entry is sixteen bytes with shared, remapped and posted views, helper copies shared subset.

Operation bundles callback, RCU successor, flags, private data, saved callback, filters with prior state, trampoline, lists, command handler, peer and direct target; hash holds RCU filters; capture is opaque with arch, partial, perf, pointer, caller and stack hooks; direct entries pair linkage with address and target.

ABI cookies signed 32-bit with one minimum and negatives errors; status complete, in-progress, paused, error, out-of-order; caps copy, xor, parity, verify, fill, scattered fill, interrupt, private, async, slave, cyclic, interleave, unordered, repeat, load-EOT plus terminator; orientations mem-mem, mem-dev, dev-mem, dev-dev, none; control bits zero to nine map interrupt, ack, parity disables, continue, fence, reuse, cmd, repeat, load-EOT.

ABI masks are bitmaps sized by terminator; metadata none zero, client first bit, engine second; residue zero to two; bus widths zero, one, two, three, four, eight, sixteen, thirty-two, sixty-four, one-hundred-twenty-eight; remapping 1024 units with bits one, two, four, eight and posted split twenty-six plus thirty-two; trace hash width ten.
